chunks: What al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn Samāʿah narrated from Wuhayb ibn Ḥafṣ, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

The salat in residence is eight rakʿahs when the sun passes the meridian, during the time between that and when two-thirds of the qāmah has gone; then when two-thirds of the qāmah has gone, you begin with the obligatory prayer.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the prayer; here referring to the prescribed devotional prayer and its associated rakʿahs
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence; the state of being settled, not traveling
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory prayer; here the required Zuhr salat
key_terms.الْقَامَةِ: the qāmah; a measure used here for determining prayer time
key_terms.ثَمَانِي: eight; the number of rakʿahs mentioned for the prayer
key_terms.ثُلُثَا: two-thirds; the measured extent marking the end of this time
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: units of prayer consisting of standing, bowing, and prostration
key_terms.زَالَتِ: declined; here meaning the sun has passed the meridian

ai.seo_question: When does the time for the eight rakʿahs before Zuhr end in residence?
ai.summary: This hadith states the timing of the supererogatory prayer before Zuhr in residence. It indicates that eight rakʿahs are prayed after the sun declines from the meridian, up to the point when two-thirds of a qāmah has passed, after which one begins the obligatory salat.
